stem: A 62-year-old retired factory worker, living with HIV and on antiretroviral therapy for several years, presents after more than three months of cough and weight loss, which she attributed to her HIV itself rather than a new problem. Her most recent CD4 count was 340 cells/uL, checked six months ago. She has never been treated for TB and has no known contact with anyone with drug-resistant TB. Sputum Xpert MTB/RIF positive, rifampicin not detected. Exam: thin, scattered crackles, no oral thrush, no lymphadenopathy.

patient.social_history: Lives with family; living with HIV, on ART for several years, followed at a local clinic
patient.presenting_complaint: Cough and weight loss, attributed initially to underlying HIV rather than a new process
patient.exam_findings: Thin, scattered crackles, no oral thrush, no lymphadenopathy, CD4 340 cells/uL (checked 6 months prior)
patient.prior_treatment: None for this episode; on established antiretroviral therapy; no prior TB treatment

distractors: Chronic cough and weight loss attributed to her underlying HIV status itself rather than a new, superimposed infectious process
Her relatively preserved CD4 count (340 cells/uL) taken as reassuring against opportunistic infection risk
Delayed presentation attributed to her being accustomed to chronic symptoms from long-term HIV management
ntep_correct_actions: Give cotrimoxazole preventive therapy to this patient regardless of her CD4 count, since she is HIV-positive with active TB.
Perform rifampicin-resistance testing on this patient's initial diagnostic specimen regardless of prior treatment history, birth/residence history, contact history, or HIV status.

Perform rifampicin-resistance testing on this patient's initial diagnostic specimen regardless of prior treatment history, birth/residence history, contact history, or HIV status.
us_correct_actions: Reserve cotrimoxazole preventive therapy primarily for HIV-infected TB patients with a CD4 count below 200 cells/uL; at her CD4 of 340 cells/uL, this framework would not routinely use it.

Order rapid rifampicin-resistance testing for this patient because her HIV-positive status independently meets one of the specific risk criteria this framework uses to decide who receives testing -- not because testing is a universal policy.
critical_error_conditions: Omitting rifampicin-resistance testing for this patient despite her established TB diagnosis
expected_divergence_points: Whether cotrimoxazole preventive therapy is given to all HIV-positive TB patients regardless of CD4 count or reserved for those with CD4 below 200 cells/uL
Whether rifampicin-resistance testing is performed as a matter of universal policy or because specific risk criteria (in this case, her HIV status) are met
